subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment constraints and next steps (SSO / KMS / logs)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Walters <sam.walters@finpartner.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment constraints and next steps (SSO / KMS / logs)

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can converge on whether Hosted / Dedicated / Private is the right fit for FinPartner: 

Summary of must-haves you called out during the call: 
- Enterprise SSO + SCIM for provisioning (SAML 2.0 preferred)
- HSM-backed key management / BYOK (FIPS 140-2 requirement for customer data keys)
- Audit log retention policy: 7+ years stored in a customer-controlled archive
- Network restrictions: private peering or on-prem connective options (no public egress for inference traffic)

High-level recommendation based on those constraints:
- Private deployment (VPC / customer-managed control plane) best meets HSM/BYOK and long-term, customer-controlled log archive requirements.
- Dedicated capacity can meet SSO/SCIM and many KMS integrations, but for certified HSM-backed BYOK and air-gapped archive retention, Private is the safer path.
- Hosted API is likely insufficient for HSM and strict network/isolation demands without migration to Dedicated/Private.

What I attached:
- finpartner_security_questionnaire.xlsx (we started filling the security questions you provided)
- finpartner_network_diagram.pdf (placeholder — please update with internal CIDR and egress expectations)
- redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (high-level SOC 2 summary; full report available after NDA)

Proposed next steps:
1) Could you confirm whether the HSM requirement is for customer-managed HSM (BYOK) vs Redwood-managed HSM? We assume BYOK.
2) Share the procurement contact (I CC'd procurement@...) and confirm any deadlines for the security review.
3) If you agree, let's schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with our Security/Infra lead (Laura) to walk through network design and KMS options.

If you want an immediate cost comparison I can have Ben produce a Dedicated vs Private delta and the rough lead times.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0128

---

From: Sam Walters <sam.walters@finpartner.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment constraints and next steps (SSO / KMS / logs)

Tessa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our security and procurement teams: 

1) HSM/BYOK: must be customer-controlled HSM (we will not accept provider-only key custody for the data encryption keys).
2) Log retention: 7 years is our baseline for audit/AML purposes. Logs must be archived to a location we control (S3 in our account or an on-prem archive).
3) Network: we require private connectivity; unfortunately, a public-hosted endpoint is a no-go.

I've attached a fuller security questionnaire (attached). Also, procurement asked for a mutual NDA and a preliminary SOW with timelines and rough pricing. Can you send NDA and SOW templates?

Sam
Sam Walters
Head of Engineering, FinPartner
sam.walters@finpartner.com

Attachment: finpartner_security_questionnaire_v2.xlsx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Walters <sam.walters@finpartner.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment constraints and next steps (SSO / KMS / logs)

Sam —

Appreciate the specifics. Short answers inline below and suggested actions.

HSM/BYOK
- Confirmed: BYOK (customer-managed keys) is required for the HSM scenario you described. Redwood Private supports HSM integrations and customer key import workflows; Dedicated supports KMS integrations (cloud KMS) but not certified customer-managed HSM attachments in the same way as Private. Given your BYOK mandate, Private is the recommended route.

Log retention / archival
- We can send logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket or push to on-prem archive via secure transfer from Private deployments. Dedicated can forward audit logs to customer targets for limited retention windows, but multi-year archive under customer control is much easier to guarantee with Private.

SSO + SCIM
- SAML 2.0 + SCIM provisioning is supported in both Dedicated and Private; we can wire up IdP metadata during the technical deep-dive.

Network/connectivity
- Private supports private peering and direct connectivity. For Dedicated we offer VPN/peering options as well, but Private gives you tighter control over egress and the control plane.

Deliverables we can provide this week: 
- NDA template (attached link)
- Preliminary SOW outline and a Dedicated vs Private pricing delta (Ben will own the numbers)
- Schedule: Laura is available for a deep-dive Tue/Thu mornings next week.

Action items for you: finalize the security questionnaire answers and confirm the procurement contact for the NDA.

Thanks —
Tessa

Attachment: redwood_NDA_template.pdf (link will be shared once procurement confirms contact)

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment constraints and next steps (SSO / KMS / logs)

Sam / team —

I'll produce a concise Dedicated vs Private cost and timeline delta by EOD Friday (09/04). For transparency: 
- Dedicated: faster to stand up (2–4 weeks) with reserved capacity pricing; supports cloud KMS and SAML/SCIM; limited HSM options.
- Private: longer lead time (6–12 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM provisioning) and higher platform fee, but meets BYOK/HSM and multiyear log archival requirements.

If procurement can share a target budget range, that will help me tailor the proposal. Otherwise I'll provide a standard estimate range and a line-item SOW we can iterate on.
